question: A resistor of resistance $R$ is connected alone to a sinusoidal AC source of **$V$ (rms)** at angular frequency $\omega$, and it consumes average power $P$. Now an **ideal capacitor** is connected **in series** with the resistor such that at the same $\omega$ its reactance satisfies $X_C=\dfrac{1}{\omega C}=R$. The source rms voltage remains $V$. What is the new average power dissipated **in the resistor**?
